sections.category: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna into ChatGPT, Codex, and the API with a three-tier price ladder, a max reasoning effort, and a subagent-driven ultra mode

bullets.body: OpenAI moved the GPT-5.6 family from limited preview to a broad rollout on July 9, shipping Sol, Terra, and Luna into ChatGPT, Codex, and the API with a clean three-tier price ladder: Sol at $5 input / $30 output per million tokens for frontier reasoning, complex coding, and multi-step agentic work; Terra at $2.50 / $15, pitched as GPT-5.5-class performance at roughly half the cost; and Luna at $1 / $6 for high-volume summarization and automation pipelines. The release also introduces a max reasoning effort setting that gives Sol its longest thinking budget and an ultra mode that fans work out to subagents for complex tasks, pushing the product line further toward orchestrated multi-agent execution rather than single-model calls. The coding-tool ecosystem absorbed the launch same-day: GitHub Copilot lit up all three tiers on July 9. With Terra undercutting GPT-5.5 pricing while matching it, the launch resets the mid-tier cost floor that competing frontier APIs price against.

sections.category: Meta starts charging for frontier AI with Muse Spark 1.1, opening its first external Meta Model API and posting top scores on tool-use benchmarks

bullets.body: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Spark 1.1 on July 9, a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic work with a one-million-token context window and upgraded coding, tool-use, and direct computer-control capability. Two structural firsts matter more than the benchmark table: Meta is charging for model access for the first time, at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 output, and it opened a public preview of the Meta Model API — the first time outside developers can call the Muse architecture directly rather than consuming it through Meta's own apps. The model posts leading scores on scaled tool use (88.1 on MCP Atlas) and professional tool use (54.7 on JobBench), squarely targeting the agentic-workload segment that OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and SpaceXAI's Grok 4.5 shipped into the same week. Meta moving from ad-subsidized free access to a priced API puts a fourth aggressive seller into the frontier-model market at a price point below every competing flagship tier.

sections.category: Microsoft puts its 100-agent MDASH scanning harness into Windows-scale production, finding 16 vulnerabilities including four critical RCEs and shifting patching toward continuous risk-driven cycles

bullets.body: Microsoft announced on July 9 that it is expanding AI-powered vulnerability management across the Windows codebase, moving MDASH — its multi-model agentic scanning harness that orchestrates more than 100 specialized AI agents across frontier and distilled models to discover, debate, and prove exploitable bugs end-to-end — onto dedicated cloud infrastructure sized for Windows-scale scanning. The harness has already surfaced 16 new vulnerabilities across the networking and authentication stack, including four critical remote-code-execution flaws in components like the kernel TCP/IP stack and the IKEv2 service. Microsoft's framing is the notable part: because AI-driven discovery now works for attackers too, it argues the industry must abandon calendar-bound patch cycles for continuous, risk-driven remediation — the defensive mirror of the same week's JADEPUFFER incident, where an autonomous agent ran an intrusion end-to-end. An OS vendor operationalizing agentic vulnerability discovery at production scale is a concrete data point for how fast the find-fix loop is compressing on both sides.

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: ICML's final workshop day lands tomorrow while the Hot Chips early-rate deadline and the August security block are the next dates to lock

bullets.body: Research first: ICML 2026 in Seoul closes out its workshop program July 10-11, so tomorrow is the last day to catch sessions on-site or remote; the next marquee research venue after it is NeurIPS in Sydney in December. For Bay Area locals, the next AI Tinkerers San Francisco meetup is set for August in the usual working-demo format, and The AI Conference returns to Pier 48 in San Francisco September 29 to October 1 with agents, infrastructure, and applied-AI tracks, while Anyscale's Ray Summit runs a late-August program for AI-infra builders. On the AI-chip and hardware track, the nearest gathering is Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford on August 23-25, whose early-registration rate closes July 31 per the Hot Chips registration page — three weeks out — followed by the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17. The AI-security block clusters in August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas in early August, OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6, and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues for teams focused on agent-hijack and MCP-layer defense. On the enterprise track, Ai4 2026 runs August 4-6 at The Venetian in Las Vegas, the ACM AI Leadership Summit is August 30 to September 2 in Atlanta, GitHub Universe is October 28-29, and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. Near-term actions: catch the final ICML workshop day July 11, lock the July 31 Hot Chips early rate, and book the August AI Risk Summit and Black Hat/DEF CON dates — with this week's GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, and Muse Spark launches, the August-September circuit is where the first hands-on agentic-deployment retrospectives will surface.
